text:
anya: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking of deprecating the old 'compat' quant profiles (v1) and adding a runtime shim that rewrites profile headers to v2 on load. Want to sync on tradeoffs (quality regression windows, auditability, rollback). Opinions? :eyes:

devon: If we auto-rewrite, we need a gated canary and per-model opt-out. Risk: subtle fp8->int4 transitions can change logits. We should run prompt-based regressions.

oliver: Prefer a negotiation layer not silent rewriting. Runtime should expose negotiated precision and a header flag so consumers can opt out. Silent changes = user surprises.

maria: From QA: add a compatibility test harness (per-model prompt-suite + BLEU/ROUGE/regression metrics). Also add upload-time warning and eventual rejection for v1.

rui: Perf implications? shim = small parse step but may force different kernel selection. Need perf microbenchmarks: seq=64/512, batch sizes. Also KV cache layout compatibility — does shim preserve cache key ordering?

perf-bot: telemetry: enabling shim on dedicated dev cluster increased p99 by ~0.9% for seq=64 on A100, mem overhead +1.2%. Quality delta (on eval suite) shows median chrF drop 0.4 points for int4 fallback cases.

devon: good data. We should define a deprecation timeline: warn -> opt-in shim -> opt-out removal. Also specify rollback path: keep v1-serving variant until confirm.

oliver: Contract: model manifest needs `precision_profile_version` and `negotiation: allow_shim: true|false`. Example:
```
model_manifest:
  precision_profile_version: v2
  negotiation:
    allow_shim: false
```

maria: ops playbook: canary on 5% traffic, monitor quality regression alerts (eval set), and a fast toggle to revert routing to v1 pool.

anya: Action items: I will update RFC with shim design + manifest field + deprecation timeline. Owners: oliver (shim), maria (canary QA), rui (perf), devon (rollout policy). I'll schedule 30m sync Wed. :+1:

oliver: :thumbsup:

maria: noted, I'll prep test suites.

rui: I'll run perf matrix and push results to the RFC doc.

perf-bot: scheduled nightly comparisons between v1/v2 with current harness. Results -> #perf-diffs channel.

anya: thanks all. Leaving this thread open for minor follow-ups.
